full_judgment:
On an application filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Party to show cause as to why the accused-petitioners should not be enlarged on bail in GR Case No. 174 of 2024, arising out of Mohammadpur Police Station Case No. 37 dated 7-2-2024, under sections 304A of the Penal Code, 1860, now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that, a very poor man named Lukesh Oran, as informant, lodged an FIR on 7-2-2024 with the Mohammadpur Police Station, alleging interalia that, through an acquaintance named Nintu, his daughter, Priti Oran (15), was employed as a domestic servant in the house of the accused-petitioners, at Flat No. 8/C, House No. 2/7. Shahjahan Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. It has also been alleged that, the informant could not frequently visit his daughter and tried to contact with her at several times, but the accused-petitioners had always denied him the visit. It has further been stated that, on 6-2-2024, at about 3-00 pm, Mintu informed him that, his daughter was very sick and was admitted into a hospital. At once, the informant and his wife rushed to Dhak, on 6-2-2024, and reached at the house of the accused at 11-00 pm and then he was informed that, his daughter had fallen through an opening of the flat and fell upon the roof of a garage and, thereafter, the Manager Abdul Adel rescued his daughter and took her to Shahid Sharawardi Hospital, where the doctor declared that she was died. The informant continued his narration that he and his wife heard that his daughter fell down from the Flat of the accused-petitioners because there was no safety net (grill) at the opening of the living space. He has also stated that, on 4-8-2023, another incident took place and a victim, namely Ferdousi (7), also fell through the said opening and died. He alleges that, owing to the negligence of the accused-petitioners his daughter had to face this fatal consequence. This has been registered as GR Case No. 174 of 2024, arising out of Mohammadpur Police Station Case No. 37 dated 7-2-2024, under sections 304A of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 4. Learned Advocate Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan appeared on behalf of the accused-petitioners. Having placed the petition and the supplementary affidavit, he first of all submits that, the case has arisen on the allegation of committing an offence under section 304A of the Penal Code, 1860, which is abailable offence. Therefore, it is statutory right of the accused-petitioner to get bail and this right cannot be curtailed by the Court, as has been held by the Appellate Division in a case reported in 68 DLR (AD) (2016) 290: between Mia Nuruddin (Apu) vs The State. He asserts that, on this ground alone the petitioner is entitled to get bail. The learned Advocate next submits that these petitioners were arrested on the date of occurrence, that is on 6-2-2024, immediately after the occurrence and before lodging of the FIR and since then the petitioner No. 1, is in jail custody and the petitioner No. 2, until 22-4-2024. when she was granted ad-interim bail by this Honfble Court at the time of issuance of this Rule. He proceeds on that, the petitioners were taken on remand one for 3(three) days, vide order dated 7-2-2024, and then again for the second time for 4(four) days, vide order dated 13-2-2024. but nothing was extracted, nor any evidence could be gathered by the police to connect them with the offence alleged. He also adds that, it is uncertain as to when the investigation will be completed and the petitioner cannot be made to suffer for no fault of them. Before concluding, the learned Advocate has drawn out attention to a letter dated 2-4-2024 of the Daily Stat, whereby the services of the petitioner No. 1 has been terminated. He submits that, the petitioner is the victim of circumstances. He however, argues that, on these counts, the accused-petitioner No. I may be granted bail and he also prays for confirmation of the ad-interim bail granted to the petitioner No. 2, since there is no allegation of misuse. He prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 9. As on today, the case remains to be one under section 304A of the Penal Code, which is a bailable offence. In view of the decision of the Appellate Division, this is a statutory right of the petitioner which cannot curtailed by the Court, vide the judgment, reported in 68 DLR (AD) (2016) 290 between Mia Nuruddin (Apu) vs The State.
